reviewedRevision: eb5efe6 plus the hardening in this commit
owner: coordinator (small hardening fix after the review)
process: Not level-based (a single match), so no retrofit. One independent review round passed it; its one MEDIUM hardening item and two cheap LOW items were fixed by the coordinator and verified by re-running the reviewer's own physics and pilot probes, one clean-worktree run and the browser check, without a second review round.
independentProbes: The reviewer's reaction-limited bot beat the computer in 30 of 30 matches at 0.25 s and 0.35 s (about 7-0); with sloppy aim it still won 27 of 30. Idle, mash, random keys and held patterns at five periods won 0 of 30 each. 800 shots from 400 to 6000 px/s at frame times up to 0.1 s produced no tunnelling. On the final file the same physics probe ran its hostile-input fuzz without a non-finite value, capped two-player ramming at 900 px/s, and reported the solo loss as 'The computer wins 2–7.'

findings.observation: A NaN pointer y while the pointer was down set a paddle's position to NaN for the rest of the match. Pointer steering now requires finite coordinates, with a regression test.

Repeated two-player ramming could pump the ball to about 32,800 px/s. Ball speed is now capped at 900 px/s (about four times the serve); the extreme-speed tunnelling test still proves the first contact returns the ball.
Found in the browser check: a solo loss read 'Player 2 wins'. Solo results now name the computer ('The computer wins 0–7.' / '电脑以0–7获胜。'), while duels keep 'Player N wins'.

openNotes: The computer is beatable but easy: a reaction-limited bot wins about 7-0, and the three CPU tiers add only mild pressure.
Purely defensive play can rally until the 45 s let and replay points, so matches can run long.
Final scores for the same scripted input differ slightly between 30, 60 and 120 Hz; the host always steps at 1/120 s.

browser.method: Official Claude in Chrome extension, local server; real clicks on Start, Play again, the language switch and the touch buttons, synthetic in-page keys; only DOM text and the canvas were read.
observed: Chinese: Start opened a solo match (电脑 1 级); W moved the paddle and Space served, and the player scored the first point before idling.
Loss: left idle, the computer won; on the final file the English overlay read 'The computer wins 0–7.' and Play again restarted at 0 : 0 against CPU tier 1.
Chinese 390 px phone frame (388 px inner, no horizontal overflow): touch buttons 上 下 发球 and the 单人/双人 mode toggle; the Serve button launched the ball.
Not covered in the browser: a full win and the two-player mode; the reviewer's bots and the quality tests cover both.
